measurements.scope: Approximate basin-wide eastward pathway from north of Papua New Guinea to the South American coast described in Grenier et al. (2011). The source's 14,000 km is a broad path estimate, not a traced instantaneous core or the length of the Atlantic or Indian Equatorial Undercurrent. A 0°N, 140°W mooring locates the current independently.

A later wave–current dynamics paper describes the Pacific EUC as traversing the equatorial Pacific over about 13,000 km. It does not define the same exact core or gates as Grenier et al.; retained as a source-specific whole-basin approximation rather than an independent rank.
measurements.source_locator: Introduction, opening Equatorial Undercurrent description, entire Pacific equatorial length about 13,000 km

map_features.note: Published April 1987 observation site at 0°N, 140°W; not a whole-current centerline or endpoint.
map_features.positional_uncertainty: not quantified; no observed current core or path

widths.boundary_rule: Author-reported approximate background width. No velocity cutoff, paired boundaries or explicit transverse section extracted. Model transport boxes are not width boundaries.
widths.extraction_method: Approximate width transcribed from visually inspected publisher original p1 prose; no map, current axis or model transport-box width digitization.
widths.geographic_scope: Pacific eastward equatorial subsurface jet; background approximation without a fixed section longitude or paired edge coordinates. Not the generic cross-basin family or Atlantic/Indian EUC.
widths.layer: Subsurface current background; adjacent approximate thickness and 50–200 m core depths are context, not a fixed width measurement layer.
widths.name: Pacific Equatorial Undercurrent

original_regional_context.display_caption: Pacific eastward subsurface jet · one approximate 400 km background width. Numerical uncertainty, width range, fixed measurement layer and observation dates unknown. Transport and velocity seasonal cycles do not supply monthly widths. No annual range or mapped edges inferred.
original_regional_context.display_method_note: Publisher p1 width prose and p4 transport context inspected. About 200 m thickness and 50–200 m core depths are separate descriptions. The 3°S–3°N transport box is not a width observation. Historical boundary method remains unreviewed; no transfer to other basin currents.
